title: User Registration with Valid Password
gherkin:
Feature: Password Policy Enforcement
  Scenario: User registers with a valid password
    Given the user is on the registration page
    When the user enters a password that meets the policy requirements
    And submits the registration form
    Then the user should be successfully registered
    And the system should store the password securely
rationale: To ensure that users can register only with passwords that meet the defined complexity and length requirements, thus enhancing security.

Subject: Registration consent flow must be revised before launch

Hi All,

During the latest compliance review, Legal raised a blocking concern regarding how consent is collected in the registration journey.

At the moment, the current approach appears to bundle multiple legal acknowledgements too closely. For launch readiness, users need to express consent to the contractual terms and the personal-data-related notice in a clearly distinguishable way. A single combined acknowledgement is not sufficient for this purpose.

Please adjust the registration flow so that these approvals are captured independently and can be demonstrated separately if needed during audit.

This is a release-blocking compliance item.

Best regards,

Dr. Arpad Jog
General Counsel

Support keeps running into cases where a high-priority customer wants to secure an item even though the system currently treats the time window as blocked because of another pending request.

Hi Dev Team,

Support keeps running into cases where a high-priority customer wants to secure an item even though the system currently treats the time window as blocked because of another pending request.

Operationally, the team is asking whether specially authorized staff should be able to intervene in those cases and resolve the conflict manually, rather than forcing the customer to wait for the ordinary availability flow to clear on its own. In practice this would mean allowing a priority booking path to take precedence over weaker, not-yet-confirmed demand.

Please do not treat this as confirmed product policy yet. We need guidance on whether this should remain a support-side exception process, or whether the booking logic itself is expected to support it.

Regards,

Subject: Escalation: exception handling for priority customers

Hi Dev Team,

Support keeps running into cases where a high-priority customer wants to secure an item even though the system currently treats the time window as blocked because of another pending request.

Operationally, the team is asking whether specially authorized staff should be able to intervene in those cases and resolve the conflict manually, rather than forcing the customer to wait for the ordinary availability flow to clear on its own. In practice this would mean allowing a priority booking path to take precedence over weaker, not-yet-confirmed demand.

Please do not treat this as confirmed product policy yet. We need guidance on whether this should remain a support-side exception process, or whether the booking logic itself is expected to support it.

Regards,
Sarah (Support Lead)
